subject: Millcross
prompt: A small walled crossing town of a dozen and a half structures on both banks of a grey river, viewed from the road at cart height, late afternoon. Whitewashed plaster-and-stone houses, their timber frames visible only at corners and doorheads, stand inside a timber-and-earth town wall under steep slate roofs, with brick chimney stacks and brick plinths at their feet; the west gate tower is plain oak with an open cart passage and black iron hinge straps, and painted emblem boards — the crossed roads over an empty bowl — hang on wrought-iron brackets along the high street. A queue of wooden ox-carts loaded with sacks, and led pack animals, fills the well-worn earth road from the foreground to the ford, the gravel ford is the only crossing, the nearest carts stand mid-stream in the shallows with water at the wheel hubs, wet wheel ruts drying on the stones, the queue longer than the town is wide. One timber mill-wheel housing stands beside the sluice at the crossing, the great wooden wheel turning in the open race, taller than the wall or any rooftop; the guild hall and the inn rise a second storey inside the wall. Beyond the gates the last house stands in open plain — beyond the town edge only the two earth roads, the ford and low farmland remain. Palette ash-grey, rope-brown, tallow-yellow; awnings along the high street chalked with a circle crossed by two strokes.
mustAssert: a dozen and a half structures
